subject: Plotting multiple plots of x against several y's in one ggplot call

messages.author: 452569198af8caee
messages.subject: Plotting multiple plots of x against several y's in one ggplot call
parts:
Hi list,

I would like to plot several x (continuous) vs. different y's (continuous), a bit like plot(dataset) in base R, but for one variable at a time. I was wondering if there is any way of doing that in only one ggplot call? I'm using melt and fact_grid to plot relations with factors, but I can't figure how it could be done with molten data in the case here (if it could be done at all).

Any idea would be appreciated.

I've made a dummy dataset, as far.

dummy = data.frame(x=rnorm(20),y1=rnorm(20),y2=rnorm(20),y3=rnorm(20))

Thank you!

guillaume

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Plotting multiple plots of x against several y's in one ggplot call
parts:
Guillaume, melt and facet grid will do. Unless you want different graphics. Consider this:

dummy = data.frame(x=rnorm(20),y1=rnorm(20),y2=rnorm(20),y3=rnorm(20))

library(reshape2); library(ggplot2)

molten.dummy <- melt(dummy, id.vars = "x")
qplot(x, value, data = molten dummy) + facet_wrap(~variable)

HTH

Luciano

messages.subject: Re: Plotting multiple plots of x against several y's in one ggplot call
parts:
Sorry, I read to quickly and didn't realize you wanted diferent plots. So borrowing from baptiste code:

dummy = data.frame(x=rnorm(20),y1=rnorm(20),y2=rnorm(20),y3=rnorm(20))

library(ggplot2)

## function to generate one plot
plotone <- function(var, ...){
 windows()
 print(qplot(x, value, data = subset(molten.dummy, variable == var,), main = var))
 
}


## loop over the variables and store all plots (5 in the example)
l_ply(levels(molten.dummy$variable), plotone)

I hope that's what you want
Luciano
